title: Seven in the morning, cups still on

tokens.v: Full-bleed photograph, edge to edge, no border, frame or letterbox band. Seven in the morning in a narrow kitchen: he stands turned almost fully away with the canvas cups on, the straight side part holding its line, only the back quarter of his head and one shoulder in frame. Camera level with his ear a metre away and swung behind him so the near cup — his left — sits square-on to the lens and owns a good third of the frame width, a pale disc against the shadowed wall. 85mm at f/2.8; low window light from the left grazes the oatmeal-beige cotton canvas so its over-under basket weave resolves warp thread by weft thread, the fine top-stitched seam encircling the cup readable, the cork headband lining granular, the matte ecru yoke arm flat and sheenless. That cup is entirely plain — no button, port, status light or lettering. The kettle's steam is the only thing between lens and product, climbing through the near-right across the cup's right edge and softening that edge alone. No hands and nothing below the chest in frame; an ecru waffle henley collar is the only wardrobe.
